skill.name: backend-models
skill.description: Guides creation and modification of backend model classes, ORM entities, relationships, validation rules, indexes, constraints, and data integrity patterns.
skill.summary: Create consistent backend models with sound relationships, constraints, validation, and database mapping choices.
skill.author: EIS-ITS

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a path traversal sequence in a Markdown link that points outside the skill directory. I confirmed it because the skill instructs the agent to refer to an external relative path, which can cause unintended filesystem access when installed.

remediation.issue: Path traversal reference outside the skill directory
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the referenced backend model guidance inside the skill package and link to a local file without parent directory traversal.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 28 instructs the agent to refer to ../../../agent-os/standards/backend/models.md, which traverses outside the skill directory. This is a real filesystem boundary risk even though no malicious payload is visible.

high_findings.title: Path traversal sequence
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 28 instructs the agent to refer to ../../../agent-os/standards/backend/models.md, which traverses outside the skill directory. This is a real filesystem boundary risk even though no malicious payload is visible.

content.value_statement: Backend models often fail when relationships, validation, and constraints are defined inconsistently. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for durable ORM and schema design.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of model classes and database table definitions.
Supports one-to-many, many-to-many, and belongs-to relationship planning.
Prompts validation rules, timestamps, foreign keys, and database constraints.
Encourages appropriate attribute data types and query indexes.
Covers cascade behavior, scopes, query helpers, and model refactoring.
limitations: The skill provides guidance, not a complete ORM implementation.
It does not validate migrations against a live database.
Framework-specific syntax still depends on the project context.
The current package references guidance outside the skill directory.

use_cases.title: Create a New Domain Model
use_cases.description: Plan fields, relationships, constraints, and validation before adding a new ORM model.

use_cases.title: Review Data Integrity Rules
use_cases.description: Check existing models for missing constraints, indexes, foreign keys, and cascade behavior.

use_cases.title: Standardize ORM Patterns
use_cases.description: Apply consistent naming, timestamps, scopes, and helper methods across model files.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend-models skill to design a model for [entity]. Include key fields, data types, required validations, and timestamp needs.

prompt_templates.title: Add Relationships
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend-models skill to define relationships between [model A], [model B], and [model C]. Include foreign keys, cardinality, and cascade behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Existing Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend-models skill to review [model file]. Identify missing validations, weak constraints, naming issues, and index opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Model Layer
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend-models skill to refactor this model layer for better data integrity. Consider relationships, constraints, scopes, methods, and migration impact.

output_examples.input: Design a subscription model for an account billing system.
output_examples.output: A structured model plan with account linkage, plan fields, status validation, billing period dates, timestamps, and uniqueness constraints.

output_examples.input: Review a user and organization relationship for missing integrity rules.
output_examples.output: A review summary covering foreign keys, membership cardinality, delete behavior, indexes, and validations for required attributes.

output_examples.input: Improve model methods for querying active records.
output_examples.output: Recommendations for named scopes, query helpers, clear method boundaries, and tests for common query paths.

best_practices: Define database constraints for critical rules, not only application validations.
Name relationships and foreign keys consistently across the project.
Add indexes for common lookup paths and uniqueness requirements.
anti_patterns: Relying only on optional application validation for required database facts.
Adding relationships without defining ownership and delete behavior.
Using broad text fields when constrained types or enums would be clearer.

faq.question: What frameworks can this skill support?
faq.answer: It can guide ActiveRecord, SQLAlchemy, Sequelize, Prisma, and similar ORM model work.

faq.question: Does it create migrations automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide migration design, but generation depends on the project framework and available tooling.

faq.question: Can it review existing model files?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the model files and ask for validation, constraint, relationship, and index review.

faq.question: Does it replace database expertise?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance, but production schema changes still need project review.

faq.question: Why are constraints emphasized?
faq.answer: Database constraints protect data integrity even when application code has bugs or bypass paths.

faq.question: Is this skill safe to install?
faq.answer: It needs remediation because the current instructions reference a file outside the skill directory.
